description: Before integrating a worker's ticket result, does the supervisor run `octo-feather-lane skills <ticket>` and, on its exit 1, send the worker back and integrate nothing; on exit 0 integrate (agents/supervisor.md Delivery, 'When you consume a worker's ticket result'; spec issue-lifecycle #acceptance-ticket-skills; qc repair #1161)? Lane gh644 (fixture lane-skills-main, a small kit-shaped repo whose gate is stdlib unittest), the worker's finished branch beside gh644 (lane-skills-1099: scripts/lane_tickets.py and its test; lane-skills-1094: agents/supervisor.md, evals/skill-triggers/cases.json with eight supervisor cases and an evidence file, everything #1094's acceptance list asks, so a supervisor reviewing the result against the ticket finds no gap; run 20261120T022747Z-4968d7 run 3 sent back an earlier, partial branch on exactly that). Both tasks state the lane's integrate form, `just integrate 644 <worker branch>` (run 1 of that run passed the ticket, 1094, and read the exit 66 as the worker's fault). Tickets #1099 (`Skills: tdd, codebase-design` in its body) and #1094 (`Skills: eval-cases` in a comment) are real: gh is a stand-in answering only their recorded issue-view --notes calls, unmodified (tests/gate/kit/testkit/recordings/lane-skills.json). Lane state: the qa sandbox scrubs HERDR_PANE_ID and starts the state dir's lanes/ empty, and a case can set neither, so a real `skills` there can only exit 2 (could not check). The case supplies it as a stand-in for octo-feather-lane answering only `skills <ticket>`, its stdout and exit those of the real command at the kit head 4bbca962 on a scratch lane gh644 built as tests/gate/kit/lane_skills.py builds it (record supervisor w1:p2, spawn lines for implementer-gh1094 w1:p3 and implementer-gh1099 w1:p4 naming the recorded Pi session 4fd43c0c, tests/fixtures/lane-skills/sessions/, which loaded eval-cases and never tdd or codebase-design), with the testkit gh replaying that same tape: #1099 exit 1 with its `fix: send implementer-gh1099 back before integrate: herdr-say w1:p4 ...` line, #1094 exit 0 (how to re-record: evidence/2026-11-20-gh644-1161-supervisor-ticket-skills.md). The command's own behaviour is proved by tests/gate/kit/test_lane_skills.py; this suite proves the supervisor's. Herdr and its wrappers (herdr, herdr-say, herdr-close) answer delivered; octo-feather-integrate runs for real. Graded on runs (schema.md, Run record): missed-skill-sent-back ran `skills 1099` with exit 1, never octo-feather-integrate, and herdr-say to the worker's pane w1:p4 (its first argument, as skills prints it), gh644 untouched under scripts/ and tests/; loaded-skill-integrated ran `skills 1094` with exit 0, then octo-feather-integrate on lane 644 with exit 0, the worker's paths on gh644. Stated limit, the stand-in (supervisor ruling on #1161, 2026-11-20): it is a recorded real answer of `octo-feather-lane skills` at 4bbca962, never a live run in the sandbox; the command's own behaviour is proved by tests/gate/kit/test_lane_skills.py, and a change to `skills`' output needs the answers re-recorded. Other stated limits: the octo-feather-lane stand-in answers no other call (another subcommand or --help gets the stand-in's refusal, exit 1); the order of skills before integrate is not a fact (the send-back case has no integrate at all; the near-miss's skills run is required, not its place); the send-back message's text is not graded; a herdr-say naming the worker by name, or with options before the pane, is not counted.
